safety_notice: A photo cannot confirm what an item contains or that it is safe to handle. Check it yourself before you start, and follow your local council's rules.

Glass: Do not use glass that is chipped, cracked or broken. Wrap broken glass in thick paper, label it and put it in general waste.
Do not cut, drill or heat glass at home.
Metal: Check rims and lids for sharp edges. Wear gloves and cover cut edges with tape before handling.
Do not reuse cans that held paint, fuel or chemicals.

Plastic.title: Self-watering planter from a plastic bottle
steps: Rinse the bottle and cut it in half around the middle.
Push a cotton string through a hole in the cap so it hangs into the bottom half.
Turn the top half upside down into the bottom, add water below and soil plus a plant on top.
precautions: Cut slowly and away from your body. Ask an adult to help with scissors.
Do not reuse bottles that held chemicals or cleaning products.

Glass.title: Storage jar from an intact glass jar or bottle
steps: Check the jar carefully for chips and cracks. Stop if you find any.
Soak it in warm soapy water, remove the old label and let it dry fully.
Label it and use it to store dry food, seeds, buttons or stationery.

Metal.title: Desk organiser from a food or drink can
steps: Rinse the can and let it dry completely.
Cover the top rim with a double layer of electrical tape.
Wrap the outside in paper or fabric and use it for pens, brushes or cutlery.

Organic.title: Start a simple compost bin
materials: Bin or box with a lid
steps: Make a few small air holes in the bin and place it outdoors on soil or grass.
Add food scraps and cover each layer with an equal amount of dry leaves or cardboard.
Turn the mix every week. It becomes compost in about two to three months.
precautions: Do not add meat, dairy, oily food or pet waste. They attract pests.
Wash your hands after handling food waste.

Hazardous.title: Store safely and take to a hazardous waste collection point
steps: Do not open, crush, puncture or burn the item. Keep it away from heat and children.
Tape the terminals of batteries, keep aerosol cans upright, and store everything in a dry box.
Take it to a battery drop-off or household hazardous waste site. Never put it in regular bins.
precautions: If a battery is swollen, hot, leaking or smoking, move away and contact your local fire service.
